title: 2022 Pymble Legal Studies Trial
notes: No answer key is included in the supplied paper; answers are reasoned guesses. Question 6 uses a cropped image stimulus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a social crime prevention method?

options.A: CCTV cameras
options.B: Electronic tags on clothing
options.C: Keeping supporters of rival teams on opposite sides of the field
options.D: A domestic violence anger management course

questions.answerNote: A behaviour-change program addresses social causes of offending.

questions.stem:
During sentencing, a judge makes the following remarks to the offender: “This sentence should serve as a warning to you”

Which purpose of punishment is the judge aiming to achieve?

options.A: Specific deterrence
options.B: General deterrence
options.C: Diversionary programs
options.D: Retribution

questions.answerNote: A warning directed to this offender aims at specific deterrence.

questions.stem: Which of the following refers to a non-parole period?

options.A: A period of imprisonment where parole cannot be granted
options.B: A non-definite period of imprisonment where parole cannot be granted
options.C: A period of imprisonment where parole can be granted
options.D: The period after the mandatory minimum sentence has been served

questions.answerNote: The non-parole period is the minimum term during which parole is unavailable.

questions.stem:
Indiyah swung around quickly such that you thought she was going to give you a “light punch.” You reacted by punching Indiyah in the face on the right-hand side. This punch proved to be fatal.

What category of crime is this an example of?

options.A: One punch laws
options.B: Public order offences
options.C: Offences against the person
options.D: Preliminary offences

questions.answerNote: A fatal assault is an offence against the person.

questions.stem: Paige is convicted of armed robbery. The Director of Public Prosecutions is now seeking to have the severity of the sentence increased to better reflect community standards. Which court will hear the appeal?

options.A: High Court
options.B: Court of Criminal Appeal
options.C: Supreme Court
options.D: District Court

questions.answerNote: The Court of Criminal Appeal hears prosecution appeals against sentence for serious indictable matters.

questions.stem: What human right is being promoted?

options.A: Universal suffrage
options.B: Climate
options.C: Peace
options.D: Environmental

questions.answerNote: Image is a 'Climate Act Now' rally with bushfire imagery; The right promoted is the environmental (collective) right. B 'Climate' is not a recognised human right, so D is preferred, though a marker could argue B.

questions.stem: What are police most likely to do if a crime is committed and the offender flees the country?

options.A: They will send police overseas to search for the offender
options.B: Nothing due to state sovereignty
options.C: Contact the International Criminal Court to investigate the crime
options.D: Seek an extradition order

questions.answerNote: Extradition is the legal process for returning a suspect or offender from another country.

questions.stem: Zach is offered a charge negotiation in return for information about other participants in the crime. Which of the following best explains the charge negotiation process?

options.A: All charges will be dropped and Zach will be released
options.B: Zach will plead not guilty and will be allowed to go free
options.C: Zach will plead guilty and the jury will pass sentence
options.D: Zach will plead guilty and the judge will likely pass a lesser sentence in return

questions.answerNote: Charge negotiations usually involve a guilty plea and may result in a sentencing discount.

questions.stem: Which of the following punishments is considered the most severe?

options.A: Periodic detention
options.B: Community Corrections Order
options.C: Conditional Release Order
options.D: Intensive Corrections Order

questions.answerNote: An Intensive Corrections Order is the most restrictive community-based sentence listed.

questions.stem: Which of the following best protects young people during the criminal investigation process?

options.A: A specialised Children’s Court
options.B: Having free access to Legal Aid until 21 years old
options.C: A support person must be present during interrogation
options.D: The prosecution can rebut doli incapax

questions.answerNote: A child suspect is generally entitled to have a responsible adult present during questioning.

questions.stem: Is the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights enforceable?

options.A: No. It is a guideline document for nation states to follow
options.B: No. It only applies to those states who have signed the UDHR.
options.C: Yes. Nation states are required to sign and ratify it
options.D: Yes. It can be enforced as it applies to all states who have signed and ratified it

questions.answerNote: The ICCPR is a treaty that is binding on states that have ratified it, so D; A and C are wrong in saying it is merely a guideline or that ratification is compulsory. Domestic enforceability still depends on implementing legislation, so no option is perfect.

questions.stem: Afia is not an Australian citizen. She has finished a 2-year prison sentence in a NSW jail. Which of the following is true?

options.A: Afia cannot be deported
options.B: The NSW Parliament must authorise Afia’s deportation
options.C: The Minister for Immigration can order Afia’s deportation
options.D: Afia must agree to be deported

questions.answerNote: Federal migration law allows the responsible Minister to cancel a non-citizen’s visa and enable removal.

questions.stem: 20-year-old Luca is facing court on a charge of car theft. Can the Children’s Court hear this matter?

options.A: No. Luca is 20 years old
options.B: No, unless he pleads guilty
options.C: Yes, if he was under 18 at the time the offence was committed
options.D: Yes, because Luca was living with his parents at the time of the offence

questions.answerNote: Children’s Court jurisdiction can depend on the accused’s age when the offence was committed.

questions.stem: Human rights are said to be inherent. What is the meaning of this?

options.A: That human rights exist from birth
options.B: That human rights apply to everyone
options.C: That human rights cannot be taken away
options.D: That no human right is more important than any other

questions.answerNote: 'Inherent' means rights belong to people from birth by virtue of being human (A). C (inalienable) is the other plausible reading, but that is a separate characteristic.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements of the criminal investigation process is in the correct order (first to last)?

options.A: Arrest, gathering evidence, bail, charge
options.B: Reporting, gathering evidence, charge, bail
options.C: Charge, arrest, gathering evidence, bail
options.D: Search, interrogation, bail, arrest

questions.answerNote: A crime is reported, investigated, charged, and then bail is determined.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about a jury’s verdict?

options.A: A jury must return a unanimous verdict
options.B: Only 10 of the 12 jurors have to agree with the verdict
options.C: A jury can return a majority verdict after 8 hours of deliberation.
options.D: A judge must direct that a majority verdict is possible before the jury retires

questions.answerNote: NSW permits majority verdicts in eligible cases after jurors have deliberated for the required period.

questions.stem: Remi raises evidence at his trial for manslaughter that he has a mental illness. How would this defence be dealt with in court?

options.A: Remi must prove it on the balance of probabilities
options.B: The evidence could only be used if the Prosecution agrees
options.C: The judge must give the jury a warning that the evidence may not be reliable
options.D: The Prosecution would only have to prove the mens rea on the balance of probabilities

questions.answerNote: The accused bears the burden of proving a mental illness defence on the balance of probabilities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a collective right?

options.A: The right to join a trade union
options.B: Self determination
options.C: The right to vote
options.D: The right to education

questions.answerNote: Self-determination is exercised collectively by a people or nation.

questions.stem: Jay is 15 years old and has been suspected of carrying drugs into a music festival. Police intend to conduct a strip search. Does Jay have the right to resist a strip search?

options.A: Yes, a responsible adult must be present
options.B: Yes, police need a warrant to conduct a strip search
options.C: No, he must follow the orders of the police officer
options.D: No, NSW police can conduct strip searches at any time

questions.answerNote: For a child, a strip search generally requires a support person unless exceptional urgency applies.

questions.stem: Davide has been fired from his job without reason. Which is true regarding his labour rights?

options.A: Davide’s trade union has the power to enforce his human rights
options.B: Davide’s trade union can further his interests but has no legal power
options.C: The International Labour Organisation governs Davide’s workplace rights
options.D: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights ensures that Davide will get his job back.

questions.answerNote: A trade union can advocate for members but does not itself hold legal enforcement power over their rights.
